title: Dual-channel co-recruitment extraction (2020 epsin osmotic dataset, observable #1 refined)
data: cmeAnalysis res.cohorts.A: 2 channels (clathrin-RFP master, epsin-EGFP slave) x 6 lifetime cohorts, ~17 timepoints, framerate 2s
scope: Conventional TIRF INTENSITY = adaptor/coat recruitment (who/how much/when), NOT curvature and NOT force. Feeds mechanism/ordering + orchestration and cross-checks the tension story.
robust_observable: epsin:clathrin peak-amplitude ratio, median over cohorts (self-normalising within a condition; raw amplitudes not comparable across files)
raw_tracks: ProcessedTracks.mat per-track trajectories NOT available (authors' original acquisition drive); worked from shipped cohort averages

wt_osmotic_tension.trend: monotonic decrease 0.84 -> 0.69 -> 0.49 with rising membrane tension

enth_deletion_control.finding: WT tension response (delta -0.34) is ABOLISHED when the ENTH curvature domain is deleted (delta +0.03): the tension-coupled epsin recruitment is ENTH-domain-specific

interpretation: Directly supports the 2020 thesis: higher membrane tension suppresses recruitment of the curvature-generating ENTH adaptor epsin relative to clathrin, and this coupling requires the ENTH domain. This is the mechanism/ordering evidence that a LINKED force claim would build on; it does not itself yield force (no curvature, no dynamics of shape).
